questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] What part of the brain controls hunger?
A. Amygdala B. Hypothalamus C. Pons
Answer: B. The hypothalamus responds to various signals in the body, including hormone levels and nutrient availability, to regulate appetite and hunger sensations.
questions.de: Welcher Teil des Gehirns steuert den Hunger?
questions.en: Which part of the brain controls hunger?

timeline.labelEn: Orexin, a hypothalamic neuropeptide that regulates feeding, is described
timeline.labelDe: Orexin, ein Neuropeptid des Hypothalamus, das die Nahrungsaufnahme reguliert, wird beschrieben

questions.notes: Confirmed: the hypothalamus controls body temperature, hunger, thirst and more. Options dropped. Timeline from the Orexin page (discovered 1998; Cell paper February 1998).

questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] The “Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis” proposes that:
A. Language determines thought and perception
B. Writing systems influenced ancient civilizations
C. Words have power only when spoken
Answer: A. This hypothesis posits that the structure of a language shapes its speakers’ worldview and cognitive patterns, influencing their perception of reality.
questions.de: Welche Hypothese, auch linguistische Relativität genannt, besagt, dass die Struktur einer Sprache das Weltbild und Denken ihrer Sprecher prägt?
questions.en: Which hypothesis, also called linguistic relativity, proposes that the structure of a language shapes its speakers' worldview and thought?

timeline.labelEn: Harry Hoijer introduces the term “Sapir–Whorf hypothesis”

questions.notes: Card's option A ('determines') is the strong version, linguistic determinism, which is now largely rejected; the explanation's weaker 'shapes/influences' is the mainstream form, so the question uses that. Sapir and Whorf never stated it as a hypothesis themselves.
